A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KOWCPI research. Text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained content to be matched despite formatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: Table 1 and Figures 2, A.1 and A.2 report original coverage and interval-width experiments on electric, wind and solar data.

after.justification: Retains the original experiments and adds stock-price, synthetic-data and adaptive-window results in Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: The RNW weighting and interval-construction algorithm remain unchanged. Appendix E implements an optional adaptive window-selection procedure using two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests between adjacent residual blocks; v1 treated adaptive selection as future work.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained electric, wind and solar datasets, v2 evaluates AAPL daily closing prices, a heteroskedastic AR/GARCH mixture and a seasonal nonstationary synthetic process. These substantially broaden the domains and temporal conditions tested.

E2.justification: The corresponding original comparisons retain all nine baselines, including Plain NW, SPCI, EnbPI and the adaptive conformal methods. SAOCF in v1's Table 1 is corrected to SAOCP. Added benchmarks use subsets of existing baselines; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The original ten-tree random forest, 7:1:2 split, coverage target and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Added setups include an 80:20 chronological stock-data split, 100-lag predictors for the seasonal simulation and a fixed-versus-adaptive window comparison.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds targeted robustness experiments under heteroskedastic volatility bursts and nonstationarity. Appendix E tests adaptive versus fixed window selection, while Figure A.3 adds a solar interval case study. The original rolling-coverage analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 reports no repeated-run counts or between-run uncertainty. V2 adds standard deviations from five independent trials to Table 1, reports three trials for AAPL and five for the nonstationary and adaptive-window studies, and presents five independent heteroskedastic paths. This establishes new reporting, not a documented increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores and rolling plots are retained. Tables A.1–A.4 add substantial results, including KOWCPI coverage/width of 0.912/15.74 on AAPL and 0.90/11.41 in the seasonal simulation. New interval and window trajectories are also reported. Table A.4 lists fixed-window electric width as 0.23, although Table 1 retains 0.22.

T1.justification: The RNW definitions, Assumptions 4.2–4.5, coverage results and Appendix A–B derivations are mathematically retained. Notation standardization, equation renumbering and explanations of the Hessian and decomposition do not change the theory.

C1.justification: The central adaptive-weighting and conditional-coverage claims remain intact. The abstract extends the empirical claim to synthetic data, and the conclusion now identifies a preliminary adaptive-window implementation where v1 discussed only future work.

C2.justification: V2 explains how residual mixing can coexist with nonstationary observations and attributes performance to rapid adaptation to volatility. Section 5 newly acknowledges brief local coverage failures from aggressive adaptation, qualifying the retained favorable interpretation.

D1.justification: Adds the AAPL data source and date range, synthetic generation equations and coefficients, and the adaptive-window testing rule with an example 0.01 threshold. It also clarifies the window-selection criterion. Existing implementation links remain unchanged; the new simulations are not fully specified, including sample lengths and the seasonal model's beta coefficients.

R1.justification: Adds Angelopoulos et al. (2024), Yang et al. (2024), and two Masry–Tjøstheim references, expanding discussion of online threshold adaptation and mixing assumptions. The central research positioning remains stable; Gibbs–Candès 2022 to 2024 is a publication update.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are preserved. V2 refines algorithm wording and explanations, standardizes notation, subdivides Appendix C, adds Appendices D–E and removes the acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn with clearer residual blocks and a PACF panel. Table 1 is expanded to display uncertainty, four appendix tables and two figures are added, and typography and page composition change throughout. Existing benchmark plots are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical support previously limited to point estimates on three energy datasets: repeated-trial uncertainty, targeted robustness tests and the adaptive-window comparison address reliability and practical tuning. The coverage-failure discussion also improves balance. New interpretations sometimes overstate the evidence—SPCI has narrower intervals with valid coverage on Table A.2's fourth path—and Tables 1/A.4 disagree on one electric width. These reporting issues temper the claims but do not outweigh the stronger empirical foundation.
